reden: Yes. The audit’s first High finding (“Guard never blocks setFallbackHandler…”) explicitly covers the same ERC1155 hijack during rental creation via the Gnosis Safe fallback handler. It states that a renter can set a fallback handler, that fallback calls bypass the Guard, and specifically that when Seaport transfers ERC1155 via safeTransferFrom, onERC1155Received is routed to the attacker-chosen handler before validateOrder/addRentals registers the rental, allowing the tokens to be moved out while isRentedOut is false. This matches the described reentrancy-based drain (tokens are sent before registration, fallback handler’s onERC1155Received enables exfiltration). While the report also notes broader abuse (post-registration bypass), it clearly detects the same creation-time ERC1155 drain mechanism described in H-03.
